Westmoreland Resources has been extracting coal under a mining and reclamation plan approved prior to the Cady vs. Morton decision. Westmoreland Resources has recently submitted a second mining and reclamation plan covering some 2,151 acres and approximately 219 million tons of coal. This application is the subject of a separate environmental statement being prepared under the leadership of the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).
DESCRIPTION OF LEASES AND HISTORY
Westmoreland Resources (a Montana based partnership owned by Westmoreland Coal Company (36 percent), Kewanee Industries (24 percent), Morrison-Knudsen Company, Inc. (24 percent) and Penn Virginia Corporation (16 percent) was the successful bidder on prospecting permits sold by the Crow Tribe of Indians at a competitive sale in 1970. The permit areas were located in what is known as the Ceded Area, north of the Crow Reservation. This area was ceded to the United States Government by the Congressional Act of April 27, 1904 (33 Stat. 352) and subsequently opened for settlement. Under the Act, Indians living on the ceded lands were permitted to remain and receive allotments on the lands they were occupying, or to move to the reduced reservation and receive payment for their former lands and the improvements thereon. After some 54 years on the market, the Congress by the Act of May 19, 1958 (72 Stat. 121), restored to Tribal ownership all of the vacant and undisposed ceded land. These lands resumed trust status and mineral rights were reinstated to the Crow Indians. The coal rights had been retained by the U.S. Government when the land in the Ceded Area was patented to the settlers, and these rights were also returned to Crow Tribal ownership
